the oracle cannot compile this entry (the prefix exists and delete forms and the SCRIP-dialect functions hash_keys, hash_values and hash_pairs do not exist in Rakudo 6: Undeclared routines), so its answer is SCRIP's to decide. The typed Hash and Pair landing (row raku-arrays-lists-and-hashes-are-typed-storage-..., hq_raku 2026-10-03) makes hash_keys, hash_values and hash_pairs return real Lists of Str and of Pair, which say prints in Rakudo's own gist forms; measured on /usr/bin/raku 2022.12 for the same values: say %h.keys prints (x), say %h.values prints (hello), say %h.pairs prints (x => hello). The old x, hello and x:hello were the SOH-joined strings' text.  [ORACLE AT PIN TIME: not consulted]

lines($path) with $path a plain Str is real-Raku's Str.lines (splits the string's OWN text), never a file-open -- verified directly against /home/resources/rakudo-local/bin/raku: lines("/tmp/x") on a file that exists WITH real content still returns ("/tmp/x",), not the file's lines; only .IO.lines or a filehandle reads the file. This entry's open($path, ':r') is SCRIP's shared Icon-style open() calling convention (a string mode positional), which real Raku's open() rejects outright (arity error) -- verified equivalent to real Raku's open($path, :r) adverb form, which the oracle runs identically through spurt/slurp/open/slurp/close. The old ref assumed lines($path) re-opens and reads the file; that was never checked against the oracle and was wrong. SCRIP's current output (path string literal, once) is the oracle-correct answer for this exact source, confirmed identical in m3 and m4; the fix that exposed it is SCRIP's by_name_dispatch.c lines() builtin, which used to wrongly fopen() a bare string argument.
